answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a bonded-stake orchard: every new identity must lock a refundable stake, like seed money buried at a cedar's roots, before it may trade or attest. The stake unlocks only after verified service history. A raven never caches food where it has not flown, so each fake identity carries a hard marginal cost — locked capital plus foregone yield. Spinning up ten thousand clones means ten thousand locked stakes; the attacker pays per identity while the network risks nothing, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational.
